QPRTase, a key degradative enzyme of quinolinac acid, was decreased in epileptic tissue.

the first degradative step of the excitotoxin and convulsant, QUIN, is decreased in human brain tissue involved in the epileptogenic process, and that the severity of the decrease correlates with the epileptogenicity of the tissue.
quinolinic phosphoribosyltransferase activity is decreased in the human epileptic brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of quinolin acid (QUIN), a convulsant and neurotoxic substance, as an endogenous factor in epilepsy.
the study of the metabolism of the excitatory amino acid neurotransmitter glutamate.
the role of excitatory amino acids and their metabolites in the pathogenesis of epilepsy.

the QPRTase is reduced in the epileptic focus and this is probably a consequence of an epileptogenic process.
a reduction of QPRAse activity is present in the epileptic focus.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the QPRTase is a good marker for the epileptic tissue.

a deficiency of the enzyme quinolinic phosphoribosyltransferase (QPRT) in human brain may contribute to the pathogenesis of epilepsy by allowing an increased concentration of the excitotoxic amino acid quinolinic (QUIN).
a reduction of QPPTase activity in epileptic human brain tissue could be one factor contributing to an increased concentration of the excitotoxic agent QUIN.

the activity of the first enzyme in the degradative pathway of QUIN is reduced in human epileptic brain.
